subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 19-year-old woman with menorrhagia is diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia and started on oral ferrous sulfate. The pharmacist advises her to take each dose with a glass of orange juice rather than with coffee or tea. Six weeks later her hemoglobin has risen from 8.2 to 10.9 g/dL and her ferritin has increased, even though the dose of iron was unchanged and she had been taking the iron on an empty stomach all along.
question: Which of the following best explains why the orange juice improved her response to iron therapy?

options.text: It increases gastric pH, which keeps iron soluble in the duodenum
It chelates iron and carries it across the intestinal brush border
It suppresses hepcidin production by the liver
Ascorbic acid reduces ferric iron to the ferrous form, increasing its absorption
Ascorbic acid converts ferrous iron to ferric iron, which is absorbed more efficiently

explanation_correct: Vitamin C facilitates iron absorption by reducing dietary ferric iron (Fe3+) to the ferrous form (Fe2+), which is the form transported across the intestinal brush border. This is why citrus juice or a vitamin C supplement is recommended with oral iron therapy. The same reducing property allows ascorbic acid to serve as an ancillary treatment for methemoglobinemia by converting Fe3+ back to Fe2+.

explanation_incorrect.A: Ascorbic acid does not raise gastric pH, and an acidic environment actually favors iron solubility and reduction.
explanation_incorrect.B: Vitamin C does not chelate iron for transport; it reduces the metal so that the divalent metal transporter can accept it.
explanation_incorrect.C: Ascorbic acid does not suppress hepcidin; that effect is not the mechanism of its benefit on iron absorption.
explanation_incorrect.E: The direction is reversed: ascorbic acid reduces Fe3+ to Fe2+, and the ferrous form is the better absorbed species.

educationalObjective: Vitamin C facilitates iron absorption by reducing Fe3+ to Fe2+, and it can also reduce methemoglobin iron back to the ferrous state.
